title: Ghost hunters wanted: Independence launches free digital passport for 13 'haunted' historic sites
excerpt: From Jesse James’ brother to a ‘woman in white,’ new tour maps Independence’s haunted history.
content:
INDEPENDENCE, Mo. (KCTV) - Ghost stories and local history are colliding this fall in Independence.

Tourism officials have unveiled the Paranormal Pursuit Passport, a free, self-guided digital tour mapping out 13 of the city’s most chilling landmarks and historic legends. The limited-time trail runs from Sept. 23 through Nov. 6, offering participants points and prizes for checking in at participating sites.

Featured locations along the trail include:

  • Vaile Mansion: Completed in 1881, the 31-room estate features reports of a woman in white—believed to be Sophia Vaile—peering through upper windows following her tragic death inside the home.
  • Bingham-Waggoner Estate: An 1852 estate where visitors and staff report phantom footsteps, a mysterious bridal figure on the main staircase, and sightings of a man in a long coat and top hat.
  • 1859 Jail & Marshal’s Home: A historic limestone jail that once housed outlaw Frank James and Confederate guerrilla leader William Quantrill, where visitors report sudden temperature drops and sightings of a fallen lawman.
  • Woodlawn Cemetery: An 1837 burial ground holding Civil War soldiers, outlaw affiliates, and the local lore of the mysterious “Lady in Gray.” Daytime-only visits are requested.
  • Pioneer Trails Adventures: A mule-drawn covered wagon outfit that offers nighttime haunted tours through historic streets and Civil War battlegrounds.
  • Historic Independence Square: Several local square shops and eateries steeped in local folklore.

“Independence has an incredible history, and with that history come generations of stories, legends and unexplained experiences,” Allison Calvin, executive director of Visit Independence, said. “The Paranormal Pursuit Passport gives visitors a fun, interactive way to discover these stories while encouraging them to explore more of our community and support local attractions and businesses along the way.”
